summary: Hyde County state fire tower known from an April 1956 newspaper report of a 4,000-acre fire nearby; no source found gives its build date or what stands today.

facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Newspaper report of about 4,000 acres of woodland burned over in Hyde County; gale winds pushed the flames from the area of the state fire tower northeast toward Swan Lake.

evidence.supports: About 4,000 acres burned over in Hyde County on a Sunday afternoon
evidence.quote: Approximately 4,000 acres of woodlands were burned over in Hyde County Sunday afternoon

evidence.supports: Winds pushed the flames from the area of the Engelhard State Fire Tower northeast toward Swan Lake, about four and a half miles
evidence.quote: pushed the flames from the general area of the Engelhard State Fire Tower in a northeasterly direction towards Swan Lake

evidence.supports: Heavy rain that followed kept the fire from burning many thousands more acres
evidence.quote: except heavy rains that followed gale winds

evidence.supports: The report is quoted from the Belhaven Pilot
Digital Collections record titled Fire Tower at Englehard, with the Englehard spelling
tnlandforms list places Engelhard in Hyde County

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Digital Collections title spells the place Englehard. The Eastern US Lookouts page and the tnlandforms list use Engelhard, and the story follows them.

sources.title: Fire Tower at Englehard
sources.publisher: North Carolina Digital Collections (North Carolina Department of Natural and Cultural Resources)

notes_for_editor: Only a 1956 newspaper item (quoted on the Eastern US Lookouts page) and the title of an undated Digital Collections record were found. The cached Digital Collections page held only its title, so its date, description and rights are unknown. Search snippets claimed the photo is credited to Charles Brantley Aycock Brown and that a Hyde County Forest Service office at Scranton has a separate tower; neither was confirmed on a page, so neither is used. The NC index lists SCRANTON as its own Hyde County entry. No build date, height, status or current condition was found.
